A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CorrGCV research and provide readable text, equations, figures, code, and appendices A–K. Content can be reliably matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V3 reports original synthetic regression experiments, including empirical risks and bias–variance decompositions in Figures 1–4 and further numerical experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: V4 retains these original experiments and adds a ridge-parameter sweep in Figure 2.

M1.justification: The ridge-regression procedure, CorrGCV estimator, and correlated-test correction are unchanged. Section 4 relocates the implementation procedure from v3's Appendix A without introducing a new algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic regression with exponential, nearest-neighbor, and power-law correlations, including structured covariates and correlated test points. The new ridge sweep uses existing coverage with different experimental parameters.

E2.justification: The standard GCV, Altman estimator, and Carmack comparison are retained. New Figure 2 uses the existing Naive GCV1 and Naive GCV2 comparators; the Carmack comparison remains in Appendix G.

E3.justification: New Figure 2 sweeps lambda from approximately 10^-6 to 1 with N=100 and q=0.91, supplementing the existing sample-size and prediction-horizon studies. Settings of the retained experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 2 adds a focused sensitivity analysis of true and estimated risks across ridge parameters, examining whether the estimators identify the risk minimum. Existing scaling, double-descent, noise-mismatch, and correlated-test analyses remain.

E5.justification: Appendix K in both versions specifies error bars over ten runs using different datasets. The repeated-run and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: New Figure 2 reports risk, bias–variance, and estimator curves across lambda, showing CorrGCV tracking the true risk and its minimum. Existing plotted results, including appendix panels, are retained unchanged; this is additional evidence rather than improved same-setting performance.

T1.justification: The numbered definition, lemmas, and theorems restate results already present in v3, with the existing appendix derivations retained. Notational cleanup, including replacing stray sample-count P symbols with T, does not change the mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: correlated-sample risk asymptotics, CorrGCV, and corrections for correlated test points. The tuning illustration supports the existing practical motivation.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 explicitly connects accurate risk estimation to identifying the optimal ridge parameter using new Figure 2. The weighted-loss discussion also specifies applicability to generalization risk Rg. Existing universality caveats and noise-matching limitations remain.

D1.justification: Figure 2 documents its new experiment's configuration, including alpha=1.1, r=0.8, correlation length 100, and noise level 0.05. The JAX code, S-transform estimation instructions, hardware description, and code-access information are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: V4 adds citations to Gu and Ma, Wang, three Xu-related works, and Atanasov et al. (2025). These modestly broaden the cross-validation context and connect the deterministic equivalents to subsequent applications without redefining the central positioning.

P1.justification: V4 promotes implementation instructions to Section 4, organizes existing mathematics into numbered statements with proof pointers, and adds author-contribution and impact statements. Most prose is retained. The relocation introduces minor reference errors, including 'Appendix CC'.

P2.justification: V4 adds Figure 2 and moves the unchanged algorithm diagram from Appendix A into the main text. V3's Figures 2 and 4 become vertically arranged Figures 3 and 6. Other plots are retained, with caption edits, renumbering, and page reflow.

improvement.justification: V3 already supplied the algorithm, theory, and extensive validation. V4 adds a useful demonstration of ridge tuning and makes the existing implementation and theorem–proof organization easier to navigate. These limited gains outweigh minor introduced cross-reference errors, while the scientific foundation remains substantially unchanged.
